significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that, at fixed mathematical problem and raw prompt-token count, higher "fragments-per-number" systematically increases thinking length without increasing necessary reasoning, and that a "fragmentation-sensitive length-budget representation" causally mediates this increase. This combines a form-(iii) predictive ordering between independently measurable fragmentation and compute with a form-(ii) mechanism, establishing both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal account; it would constrain tokenizer and benchmark choices in token-budgeted reasoning systems of the kind studied in DeepSeek-R1 and s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling. A verified-false result would informatively rule out numeral fragmentation as this particular source of spurious compute allocation, although it would not rule out other surface-form contaminants or broader explanations of overthinking. True and false are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: replacing the specific controlled fragmentation relation with the generic efficient-reasoning topic would remove the law and causal explanation that support an above-median rating.

reach.justification: The claim names both an ex-ante measurable handle, "fragments-per-number," and an input-side intervention: "re-encoding the same numbers into fewer, cleaner tokens," which can be applied before generation and therefore leaves an action window to reduce compute. After tokenizer-specific remeasurement, the directional relation still predicts that more fragmentation will produce longer reasoning, while the exact effect size and the internal steering direction would require model-specific calibration. The asserted scope covers numeral-bearing mathematical reasoning across reasoning-model families and tasks, with downstream use by benchmark designers, inference practitioners, auditors, and tokenizer designers, but it does not claim comparable effects for nonnumeric reasoning or every tokenizer. The topic-substitution check supports the score: generic mechanistic work on efficient reasoning would not itself supply this prompt-time screen and preprocessing rule, so the reach comes from the claim rather than the topic.
